title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
summary: Find the cheapest way to climb past the top of a staircase when every step you stand on has a price.

tests.explain: Start on step 1 (index 1), pay 15, and jump two steps to the top.
Step on the 1s and skip every 100 by jumping over it: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.

hints: Standing on step i costs cost[i], and from there you may move up 1 or 2 steps. The top is the position just past the last step, and you may start on step 0 or step 1.
Let best[i] be the minimum cost to arrive at position i (before paying for step i). You arrive at i from i - 1 (paying cost[i-1]) or from i - 2 (paying cost[i-2]).
best[0] = best[1] = 0, and best[i] = min(best[i-1] + cost[i-1], best[i-2] + cost[i-2]). The answer is best[n]. Only the last two values matter, so two variables are enough.
